input: a and b are nonempty strings consisting only of ASCII 0 and 1, each with no leading zero except the representation "0". Their lengths are at most 4294967294 so an extra carry digit fits a JavaScript Array. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The canonical binary string for the nonnegative sum of a and b. Output is most-significant digit first; "0" plus "0" returns "0". Arbitrarily long admitted strings are added digitwise, without parsing the represented integers into a bounded numeric type.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. A private reversed-digit sequence is allocated, reversed in place, then joined. No caller-owned sequence is modified. The returned string is immutable; object-identity freshness for equal strings is not claimed.
numeric: Each input digit contributes 0 or 1, carry is 0 or 1, and total is in [0, 3]. Modulo 2 and floor division by 2 are exact. Lengths, indices and the maximum output length remain safe integers. No bitwise operation, BigInt or whole-value arithmetic is used.
complexity: O(max(len(a), len(b))) time and auxiliary space, including construction, reversal and joining of the digit sequence. The immutable output string also has O(max(len(a), len(b))) length. Exactly one iteration consumes one right-to-left digit position and, if needed, one final carry.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 584 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs. TreeNode, where used, is an explicit caller-owned input shape and no node is constructed. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source; method-style interface parity with frozen sources remains unqualified.
